overview: The Committee reviewed comprehensive district assessment data and outlined strategies for academic rigor while approving an April vacation camp and a process for updating committee rules.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: Approved a motion to enter executive session to discuss contract negotiations for the superintendent of schools.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved routine business including bills, payroll, grants, and a $2,000 PTO donation for athletic mats.

items.title: Mustang Moment: Middle School Select Band
items.summary: Students from the Middle School Select Band performed three musical pieces and presented personal testimonials regarding the impact of the music program on their education.

items.title: MCAS Results and Accountability Report
items.summary: Administrators presented 2025 assessment data showing moderate progress toward state targets while highlighting persistent performance gaps between low-income students and their peers. The report detailed an 'instructional vision' focusing on high-quality materials and grade-level tasks to move beyond national trends where students earn high grades on below-grade-level assignments.

items.title: MAPS April Vacation Camp Approval
items.summary: Approved a four-day April vacation camp at the Brooks School utilizing a sliding scale fee structure.

items.title: New Business: School Committee Rules
items.summary: Approved Resolution 2026-6, which establishes a timeline for members to submit and review amendments to the committee's governing rules by March 2026.

items.title: Condolences
items.summary: Recognized the passing of former school crossing guard Linda C. Magaldi Iacona and longtime cafeteria worker Mary Ann Cerrone Mahoney.
